answers.answer: Build three separately shuffled tiers: the top card is 1 randomly dealt Conflict I; next are 5 randomly dealt Conflict II; bottom are all 4 Conflict III in shuffled order. Return all unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘final order from top to bottom’ is 1 Conflict I, 5 Conflict II, all 4 Conflict III; ‘Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.’

answers.answer: Each human starts with 2 Agents on the Leader and the third Agent (Swordmaster) next to the board; 3 troops in their garrison and 9 in supply; 1 water; one cube at the bottom of each of the four Influence tracks; and 0 VP in a three-player game versus 1 VP in a four-player game.
answers.evidence: Setup: 2 Agents on Leader, third Agent is Swordmaster; 12 troop cubes, 3 in garrison and the rest in supply; each player takes 1 water and places 4 cubes on bottom Influence spaces; Score track starts at 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0.

answers.answer: Yes. You may take your Reveal turn while Agents remain. After taking it, your turns are skipped for the rest of the Player Turns phase, so you cannot take another Agent turn. Plot Intrigue may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turns, so you cannot play one later in the phase after your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: ‘Agent turns are optional: you may take your Reveal turn while you still have Agents left’; after a Reveal turn ‘your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase.’ Plot cards may be played during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up and choose one Agent icon on it that matches the destination space; the card can send only one Agent, and a card with no Agent icon cannot be used for an Agent turn. Send one Agent to an unoccupied space and meet its requirements and pay its costs. Costs are paid immediately before resolving any space or card effects; if you cannot pay, you cannot go there.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: ‘play one card from your hand face up’; choose only one matching Agent icon, one card cannot send multiple Agents; space must be unoccupied; ‘Costs are paid immediately, before resolving any effects.’

answers.answer: No. The entry cost must be paid before any effects of the space or played card resolve, so an Agent card's spice gain cannot fund Conspire's 4-spice entry cost when you have only 3 spice. After legally entering and paying the cost, resolve the board-space effect, the card's Agent box, and the Faction Influence advancement in any order.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: costs are paid immediately before resolving any effects; gain the space, Agent box, and Faction advancement ‘in any order, after paying the entry cost.’ Conspire costs 4 spice.

answers.answer: You may deploy all 3 troops recruited this turn (2 from the space and 1 from the card), plus up to 2 more from your garrison, for a maximum of 5. Recruited troops you do not deploy go to your garrison. Rally Troops is not a Combat space, so its recruits go to your garrison and cannot normally be deployed there.
answers.evidence: Deploying: at a Combat space deploy ‘any or all troops you recruited this turn ... plus up to two more troops from your garrison’; recruits not deployed go to garrison. Rally Troops is ‘not a Combat space.’

answers.answer: In order: reveal all cards remaining in hand, kept separate from Agent-turn cards; resolve the Reveal boxes of those revealed cards (not boxes of cards played during Agent turns); set Combat strength; clean up. At cleanup, all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn lists four steps: Reveal Cards, Resolve Reveal Effects, Set Strength, Clean Up; Clean Up puts all cards in front of you ‘from your Agent and Reveal turns’ into your discard pile.

answers.answer: Yes, the Imperium Row refills immediately, and you may acquire the replacement if you can afford it. Persuasion from multiple sources may be pooled for one card and a single source may be split across cards. Unspent Persuasion is lost, and an acquired card goes to your discard pile rather than being usable immediately. An Acquire box resolves once, at the moment you acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards: refill the Imperium Row immediately, so you may acquire its replacement; Persuasion can be pooled or split; it cannot be saved; acquired cards go to discard; an Acquire box takes effect ‘at the moment you acquire the card.’

answers.answer: Strength is 10: 3 troops are worth 6 and 4 swords are worth 4. If your last troop is removed, strength becomes 0 and cannot be increased by any means, including swords. Above 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Set Strength: each troop is 2 strength and each revealed sword is 1; with no troops strength is 0 and cannot be increased, including by swords; over 20 use the +20 side and start again.

answers.answer: Starting with the First Player and continuing clockwise, each player with at least one troop in the Conflict may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass. Passing once does not bind you on a later opportunity. Resolve combat after all involved players pass consecutively. Play ‘when you win a Conflict’ cards only after you have won, before moving to the next phase.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue cards: players with at least one Conflict troop act from First Player clockwise; may play any number or pass; ‘not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; resolve after consecutive passes; win-trigger cards after winning, before next phase.

answers.answer: A and B tie for first, so neither wins and each receives the second reward. C and D then compete for third; C receives the third reward and D receives none. A tie for second gives each tied player the third reward, even in two- or three-player games; a tie for third gives nothing. A player with 0 strength receives no reward. After rewards, all troops in the Conflict return to their owners' supplies, not garrisons.
answers.evidence: Tied first: no winner, each tied player gets second reward; in a 4-player game the other two still compete for third. Tied second gets third reward each; tied third gets nothing; 0 strength receives no reward; troops go to supply.

answers.answer: Normal harvesting resolves when an Agent is sent to a Maker space: Imperial Basin gives 1 spice plus bonus, Hagga Basin 2 plus bonus, and The Great Flat 3 plus bonus. In Phase 4: Makers, check those three spaces and add 1 bonus spice to each that has no Agent. If an Agent moves away before Makers and the space is empty then, it receives bonus spice.
answers.evidence: Board spaces list the base harvests and accumulated bonus. Phase 4 checks The Great Flat, Hagga Basin, and Imperial Basin; if a space has no Agent, place 1 spice. Maker-spaces clarification says bonus accumulates if an Agent moves away and it is still empty in Phase 4.

answers.answer: The game ends at the end of a round during Recall if anyone has 10 or more VP or the Conflict Deck is empty. Reaching 10 mid-round does not end play immediately; the end condition is checked at Recall. The last Conflict being revealed empties the deck, so the game ends at that round's Recall. First, players may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue cards; then the player with the most VP wins. Tiebreaks are spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, then the player who most recently took a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Recall checks for 10+ VP or empty Conflict Deck; Scoring says the trigger is at end of round. Endgame Intrigue resolves first. Tiebreak order: spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, most recent Reveal turn.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence you gain 1 VP; it is lost if you drop below 2 and regained if you reach 2 again. The bonus at 4 Influence is not returned if you later drop below 4, and may be earned again by dropping and re-advancing. The first player to reach 4 takes the Alliance and its VP. A player takes it from the holder by rising to a higher Influence space; merely tying the holder does not take it.
answers.evidence: Faction Influence: 2 Influence gives a VP lost below 2 and regained at 2; the 4-space bonus is kept after dropping and can be earned again. Alliances: first to 4 takes it; an opponent rising to a higher space transfers it; merely tying does not.

answers.answer: If you lose 1 Influence while tied at 5 with two opponents, one of those previously tied opponents takes the Alliance; if several were tied, you choose which one. If instead you were the only player at 4 and fall to 3, you lose the Alliance; with no player at 4 or more to take it, return it to the board.
answers.evidence: If the holder loses Influence while previously tied, the previously tied player takes the token; if several were tied, the holder chooses one. Falling to 3 or less loses the token; if no player has 4+, return it to the board.

answers.answer: Discarding means a card from your hand unless otherwise specified, and it goes to your discard pile. Trashing permanently removes a card from your hand, discard pile, or in play to the box; a trashed Reserve card returns to its Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or a card directs you to trash itself. You may not reshuffle early just to inspect the top card of an empty deck; reshuffle only when unable to draw.
answers.evidence: Trashing cards: discard is from hand unless specified and goes to discard; trashing removes from hand, discard, or in play to the box (Reserve returns to stack); trashing is optional except for a cost or mandatory self-trash. Deck exhaustion says you can't reshuffle early to look at the top of an empty deck.

answers.answer: While you control Arrakeen or Carthag, you gain 1 Solari whenever any player, including you, sends an Agent there; control of Imperial Basin gives 1 spice on any player's visit. Winning a Conflict titled for one of those spaces lets you place your Control marker there, replacing an opponent's marker. Later, when a Conflict card is revealed for a space you already control, you may deploy one troop from your supply to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Control: a win on an Arrakeen, Carthag, or Imperial Basin Conflict places/replaces the marker; controller receives the stated bonus whenever any player visits; when a matching Conflict is revealed, deploy one troop from supply.

answers.answer: Use an unused color; put one cube at the bottom of each of the four Influence tracks and remaining cubes in its supply, with no troops in its garrison. Remove the three Arrakeen cards marked ‘1P,’ shuffle the remaining House Hagal cards, and place its deck and three Agents by its supply; use no Rival Leader or solo difficulty rules. In every standard two-player game it is a third Rival. After each First Player Agent turn, it takes one Agent turn if it has one in supply; it does not act after the other human's turn or a Reveal turn, never Reveals, and its Agents return to supply at Recall. It collects no resources, earns no Conflict rewards, scores no VP, and cannot claim Control; it can hold Faction Alliances and deny their VP to humans.
answers.evidence: Two-player House Hagal setup and Agent turns specify the unused color, cubes, no garrison troops, removal of 1P cards, shuffled deck and three Agents; actions after each First Player Agent turn; never a Reveal turn. Rival overview says it collects no resources, earns no Conflict rewards or VP, cannot claim Control, but can take and hold Alliances.

answers.answer: If the revealed card's indicated space is occupied, keep revealing until an eligible unoccupied space appears. Reshuffle immediately if its deck is empty or a Reshuffle card appears, then continue. Ignore the space's normal costs, requirements, and effects; resolve only the revealed card's icons and instructions. Each troop icon recruits from supply: deploy the troop if this is a Combat space, otherwise put it in garrison. Whenever Hagal sends an Agent to a Combat space, also deploy up to two garrison troops even if it recruited none. Harvest Spice follows its card instructions; remove harvested bonus spice from the space and return it to the bank. If a two-space card's condition selects an occupied option, draw a new card instead of switching options.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Agent turns: occupied space means reveal again; reshuffle on empty deck or Reshuffle; ignore normal space costs/requirements/effects; troop icons recruit/deploy or garrison; any Combat space permits up to two more from garrison; Harvest Spice bonus is removed and returned to bank; two-space card cannot switch options if its matching option is occupied.

answers.answer: At the start of Combat, if Hagal has a troop in the Conflict, reveal a Hagal card and add only its sword icons to its normal 2 strength per deployed troop; if it reveals Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans may play Combat Intrigue before resolution. Hagal receives no reward for its rank but occupies that rank for human reward placement. If Hagal wins a Conflict for a space a human controls, remove that Control marker and do not replace it. Human players tied for second each receive the third reward, even though an ordinary third-place finish pays nothing in a two-player game.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Combat: reveal a card if it has Conflict troops, add only swords to normal 2 per deployed troop; Hagal receives no reward but occupies its rank; remove a human Control marker if Hagal wins that space. A tie for second pays the third reward to each tied human; ordinary third place pays nothing.
